items.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: worked with a band working in a night club six nights a week and traveling, the Jim Cullum Jazz Band in San Antonio. So I was with them for 17 years.

ctx.x: And your father was supportive in you guys going in this direction?

Yeah, very much so. I worked with so many friends who tell me how their parents were very much opposed to them going into becoming professional musicians because this business is a crap shoot. Whether or not you’re going to be able to make a living at it is very questionable, and a lot of guys can’t make a living at it. I have to say that I consider myself fairly lucky. When I was 22 I took a steady job, stayed there for 17 years, and worked with a band working in a night club six nights a week and traveling, the…

Someone was asking me the other day what’s the definition of making it big? Sometimes kids use that phrase. And I think you almost just defined it. If you’re doing what you love, that’s a big step right there.
